skill.name: what-worked
skill.description: Work out what a person's best-performing Twitter or LinkedIn posts have in common, and turn that into what to write next. Use when someone asks why a post did well or badly, what their best posts have in common, what to write more of, or wants their recent posts reviewed against their numbers. Do not invent engagement numbers, and do not use this to analyse someone else's account.
skill.summary: Compare your Twitter or LinkedIn posts using real engagement data and turn supported writing patterns into ideas for your next posts.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Find What Works in Your Social Posts
content.value_statement: Raw engagement counts can hide which writing patterns perform well in your own posts. This skill compares real metrics and suggests next posts from supported patterns.
actual_capabilities: Request ten to fifteen recent posts with their text, impressions, reactions, and comments.
Compare engagement per impression when impression counts are available.
Account for post format, post age, and unusual outliers before comparing performance.
Compare stronger and weaker posts by opening line, structure, purpose, subject, and invitation to reply.
Suggest three to five next-post ideas and opening lines after the user agrees that a pattern is supported.
Describe using connected VoiceMOAT analytics tools and checking the last sync date when those tools are available.
limitations: Analysis depends on supplied metrics or an available account connector; the skill includes no connector implementation.
Small samples support tentative observations, not reliable causal explanations or guaranteed future performance.
The workflow is limited to the user's own account and does not include full post drafting unless requested.
The skill states that VoiceMOAT requires Pro or Enterprise and that LinkedIn metrics depend on browser extension sync freshness.

use_cases.title: Review Personal Twitter Posts
use_cases.description: Compare your recent posts and identify which opening lines and structures recur among stronger performers.

use_cases.title: Refine Personal LinkedIn Content
use_cases.description: Use your own post metrics to separate format and age effects from possible writing patterns before choosing future topics.

use_cases.title: Plan Posts From Connected Analytics
use_cases.description: Review your connected VoiceMOAT account for a chosen window, check data freshness, and confirm patterns before requesting new ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Post Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review my recent Twitter posts. Ask for the post text and metrics you need before drawing conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Recent Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my posts below: [posts and metrics]. Compare engagement per impression where possible, separating formats and post ages.

prompt_templates.title: Turn an Agreed Pattern Into Ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: I agree with this pattern from my posts: [pattern]. Suggest three to five ideas on [subjects I know] and matching opening lines.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: translate a confirmed observation into next-post options.

prompt_templates.title: Review Connected Account Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my connected VoiceMOAT account, review [date window]. Check sync freshness, separate outliers, and explain evidence strength before asking me to confirm patterns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: use available connected tools without treating stale data as poor performance.

output_examples.input: My two comparable text posts received 400 likes from 90,000 impressions and 60 likes from 3,000 impressions. Which performed better?
output: The second post performed better by likes per impression despite receiving fewer total likes.
Two posts are not enough to establish a repeatable writing pattern.
Please share the post text, ages, and additional comparable posts before we infer what worked.

output_examples.input: My stronger posts open with a specific lesson from client work. I agree that this is the pattern. Suggest what to write next.
output: Idea: Describe a client assumption you tested. Opening: The question that changed this project came before the work started.
Idea: Explain a decision you reversed. Opening: I changed my recommendation after one client conversation.
Idea: Share a practical lesson from a difficult handoff. Opening: The handoff exposed a problem we had missed during planning.

best_practices: Provide ten to fifteen posts with text, impressions, reactions, comments, format, and publication dates when available.
Check comparison windows and sync freshness before interpreting low activity or ranking recent posts.
Confirm the proposed writing pattern before requesting ideas, and treat small samples as tentative evidence.
anti_patterns: Inventing missing engagement numbers or substituting unsupported industry benchmarks.
Ranking different formats or post ages by raw reactions without accounting for impressions and outliers.
Analyzing another person's account or treating one unusually successful post as a guaranteed formula.

faq.question: Do I need a VoiceMOAT account?
faq.answer: No. The main workflow uses posts and engagement numbers you paste from your own Twitter or LinkedIn analytics.

faq.question: How many posts should I provide?
faq.answer: The skill asks for ten to fifteen recent posts. It can work with fewer, but should explain the limits of that sample.

faq.question: What happens when impressions are missing?
faq.answer: Engagement per impression cannot be compared without impression counts. The skill should acknowledge missing data rather than invent numbers.

faq.question: Can I use this to analyze a competitor?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly limits the workflow to the user's own account.

faq.question: Will it write complete posts?
faq.answer: It suggests ideas and opening lines after you confirm a pattern. Full drafting requires an explicit request and is directed to another workflow.

faq.question: Are connected LinkedIn metrics always current?
faq.answer: The skill states that VoiceMOAT uses browser extension sync for LinkedIn metrics. Check the last sync date before interpreting results.
